auditedPrs.notes: Squash commit 719aa88 on main. The PR cites no upstream Go. Its counterpart is the netstack link endpoint in wgengine/netstack, read at the pinned commit e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55. The PR adds a 4096-packet, 4096*MTU-byte inbound ring in front of the smoltcp netstack. It drops what does not fit, and the egress side stays unbounded. Upstream does the reverse on both sides. Inbound packets go straight into gVisor on the caller's goroutine, with no queue and no queue-full drop. Outbound packets go into a queue of 512 per outbound queue, and a writer blocks there when it is full. The bounding code itself looks correct: the byte budget is released on every refusal path, and buffered_rx is never filled, so no budget leaks. The seven new tests call the production code: WakingPipe::ingress_bounded, try_send, WakingPipeDev::receive/transmit, piped_ingress_bounded and pump_ingress. All seven passed in the gate run. Both directions differ from upstream, which gives two findings, both minor. Neither changes what a peer sees on the wire: TCP recovers dropped segments and UDP is lossy by contract. A second reading of the same squash commit judged the ingress drop a fair stand-in for Go's synchronous backpressure, because this tree's dataplane-to-transport channel is unbounded and upstream's netstack also drops silently when it is not ready, so it filed only the egress gap. The ingress finding stands anyway: #587's drop is logged only at debug level and its count is thrown away, where Go counts its inbound drops in tstun's inboundDroppedPacketsTotal.

gate.detail: Scoped gate on main 719aa88 with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4 and TS_RS_EXPERIMENT set. Every stage that ran exited 0. 1) cargo +nightly fmt --check. 2) cargo run -p checks. 3) cargo clippy --workspace --exclude ts_cli_util --lib --no-deps --all-features -- -D warnings. 4) The same clippy over bins/tests/benches/examples with -D warnings -A missing_docs. 5) cargo nextest run -p geiserx_ts_control -p geiserx_ts_runtime -p geiserx_ts_netstack_smoltcp --all-features --no-fail-fast: 998 passed, 3 skipped, including all 7 tests #587 added. ts_netstack_smoltcp was added to the nextest scope because #587 adds tests there. 6) cargo build --workspace --exclude ts_cli_util --all-targets --all-features. The 3 skipped tests were filtered out on purpose because they need sockets this sandbox blocks: serve_path_proxy_replays_consumed_head_to_backend and proxy_with_prefix_writes_prefix_before_bidi_copy hang on a dropped loopback SYN, and probe_stun_servers_once_sends_binding_request needs outbound UDP. Not run: the full bin/check, because cargo deny check all refuses aws-lc-rs/aws-lc-sys on every branch, so the set -e script stops before nextest, and ts_cli_util's tracy feature does not compile under --all-features on this host. Also not run: cargo doc, cargo machete and the doctests.

findings.title: Netstack ingress drops on a full ring where upstream delivers inbound packets synchronously, with no queue
findings.detail: Upstream: tstun.Wrapper calls the netstack's PostFilterPacketInboundFromWireGuard hook (netstack.go line 444). That hook, Impl.injectInbound (line 1433), passes an accepted packet to linkEndpoint.gro / injectInbound (netstack.go line 947; link_endpoint.go lines 238-251). That calls the gVisor dispatcher's DeliverNetworkPacket directly on the WireGuard receive goroutine. No ingress queue exists, so a packet that passed the filter is never dropped for lack of queue room. Load is limited by backpressure on the inbound path, and only gVisor's own per-endpoint limits can shed it. Merged: pump_ingress (ts_runtime/src/netstack_actor.rs) puts packets into a 4096-packet, 4096*MTU-byte flume ring with try_send. It drops any packet that does not fit, after the packet was decrypted and passed the filter. The drop is logged only at debug level, and the drop count pump_ingress returns is thrown away by both production callers (netstack_actor.rs and forwarder_actor.rs). So no metric records it. Upstream's own inbound drops are counted in tstun's inboundDroppedPacketsTotal user metric (net/tstun/wrap.go line 247). The PR's reason for dropping instead of waiting is real: the dataplane queue upstream of the pump is an unbounded mpsc: OverlayFromDataplane is mpsc::UnboundedReceiver (ts_runtime/src/dataplane.rs line 147). That is a structural difference from upstream, though, not a port of it. Fixing it means either bounding the dataplane queue so backpressure can reach the underlay, the way Go's synchronous delivery does, or recording this as an intentional fork divergence and exposing the drop count as a metric.

findings.title: Netstack egress stays unbounded where upstream caps each outbound queue at 512 packets with backpressure
findings.detail: Upstream: newLinkEndpoint(512, ...) (netstack.go line 413) gives each outbound queue a 512-slot channel (link_endpoint.go lines 144-163). queue.Write (lines 64-77) blocks the gVisor writer until a slot frees or the queue closes. WritePackets (lines 358-385) stops a batch early on ErrNoBufferSpace. So upstream's stack-to-WireGuard queue is bounded in memory, and the stack is held back while it is full. Merged: WakingPipe::ingress_bounded keeps the device-to-caller direction on flume::unbounded, and the new test egress_is_not_bounded makes that a guarantee. The doc comment says smoltcp's TxToken::consume cannot wait, so a bounded egress would stall the poll loop. smoltcp has a non-blocking way to push back, though: Device::transmit returns Option<TxToken>, and a None makes the interface defer emission to a later poll. WakingPipeDev::transmit (ts_netstack_smoltcp/src/pipe.rs) returns None only when the receiver has disconnected, never when the queue is deep. Replies a peer can provoke, such as RSTs, ICMP and ACKs, UDP replies relayed back to a peer through an exit node, plus local application sends, can therefore pile up without limit when the dataplane drains slower than smoltcp emits. That is the same memory-growth class this PR set out to close on ingress, and upstream bounds it. Porting it means bounding the egress channel and having transmit() return None while it is full, the smoltcp form of upstream's blocking queue.Write.
